title: Konstera Agent Manifest v3
description: The contract between an agent package and the Konstera kernel. Per ADR-011 §1: elevated to a validated first-class contract. Validated at upload time (POST /api/packages) and by `konstera validate` CLI. Field naming is camelCase to match existing repo convention.

manifestVersion.description: Fixed at 3 for this schema. Older manifests (v2) remain readable by the kernel but the platform warns and disables v3-only features (see ADR-011).

icon.description: Emoji or absolute image URL. Portal auto-detects.

groupName.description: Portal grouping (Finance, Reference, …). Overrides tenant default if set.

healthPath.description: HTTP path for kernel readiness probe.

timeoutSeconds.description: Invocation timeout used by the kernel HTTP client.

memoryMi.description: Container memory cap in MiB. Null uses platform default.

cpuMillis.description: CPU cap in millicores (1000 = 1 core). Null uses platform default.

pidsLimit.description: Max processes/threads. Null uses platform default.

llmRequirements.description: Abstract LLM capabilities the agent needs. Tenant admin binds each purpose to a concrete model in the portal Providers page (per ADR-011 §2).

suggestedModel.description: Optional hint the tenant admin sees when binding.

connectionRequirements.description: DEPRECATED per ADR-013: prefer `capabilities.needs[]` (canonical capability catalog) over acceptable-type lists. Kept for backwards-compat with older agents.

capabilities.description: ADR-013 capability layer — agent declares abstract capabilities it needs from the platform catalog; operator binds each to a concrete connection in the portal at install time. Same image serves many delivery models (retail / SaaS / hybrid).

needs.description: The capabilities this agent asks for. Names must exist in the platform catalog (validated at package upload). Required capabilities must be bound before the agent can be enabled; optional capabilities disappear from ctx.capability.available() when unbound.

name.description: Canonical capability key from the platform catalog (e.g. 'orders.lookup_by_email').

required.description: Whether this capability must be bound for the agent to be enabled.

reason.description: Human-readable justification shown to the operator when they bind this capability.

contextRequirements.description: ADR-038: declare context names (glossary terms, skills, ontology entities) the agent reads at runtime. The install flow cross-references these against the tenant's active Context Service repo; required names block install until present, recommended names warn. Rows written to agent_context_dependencies for the reverse-index view. All sections optional.

glossary.description: Glossary terms the agent calls ctx.semantic.glossary_lookup on. required: breakage if missing. recommended: graceful degradation.

skills.description: Skills the agent calls ctx.semantic.skills_get on. Required skills block install; recommended ones unlock richer paths when present.

ontologyEntities.description: Named ontology entities the agent reasons about (customer, order, refund, …).

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema describing what the agent returns in AgentResponse.structured. Drives the dynamic output UI renderer.

heroField.description: Top-level field name to render prominently.

heroLabel.description: Label shown with the hero value (portal default: prettified heroField).

kpiFields.description: Dot-paths rendered as secondary KPI tiles.

uiComponent.description: Escape hatch: name of a bespoke React component to render instead of generic renderer.

reviewActions.description: Custom actions the Reviewer Inbox renders for approvals this agent submits (ADR-010 Pass C; ADR-029 adds shortLabel, icon, confirm, actionType, target and payload). Targets are slot names the tenant binds to a connection; URLs and secrets never go in the manifest.

label.description: Full label; shown as the tooltip when shortLabel is set.

confirm.description: Question asked before the action runs.

actionType.description: agent: the decision goes back to the agent (on_decision). email: sent through the agent's email.send binding. webhook / api: a JSON POST through the HTTP endpoint connection bound to target.

target.description: Action slot name; required for email, webhook and api. The tenant binds it to a connection on the agent's Bindings tab.

payload.description: JSON body template. String values may contain {{ var }} with var one of approval.id, approval.kind, draft.content, detail.<key>, thread.id, thread.subject, inputs.<field>, reviewer.id. No other expressions.

review_context_panels.description: ADR-026: the agent's default Reviewer Inbox context panel. Up to four widgets in fixed slots (header, primary, secondary, footer), at most one per slot; each widget is fed by one read-only capability the manifest declares in capabilities.needs[]. A panel whose capability isn't bound for an instance is not shown. A per-instance override (agent_review_panel_overrides) replaces this list entirely. Snake_case key as written in ADR-026.

capability.description: Capability key; must be declared in capabilities.needs[].

args.description: Arguments for the capability. String values may contain {{ thread.* }}, {{ widget.<slot>.* }} or {{ tenant.* }} templates (resolved by the portal).

errorHandling.description: Circuit-breaker parameters. Defaults live in HealthTracker; manifest overrides.

triggers.description: How this agent gets invoked beyond direct sync/async API calls. Platform-provided, agent-declared.

kernelServices.description: Informational — actual enforcement is per-MCP-call. Helps portal describe agents accurately.

eval.description: ADR-044: evaluation contract. Platform's quality-check harness runs each scenario against this agent, compares the response to the expected result, and reports pass/fail per scenario and per scenario group. Omit the block entirely to opt an agent out of evaluation (fine for one-shot connectors or pure data transforms). Agents that DO opt in make their eval story portable across first- and third-party authorship — the kernel reads this block, no source-code access required.

endpoint.description: HTTP path the harness POSTs each scenario's `input` to. The agent returns a JSON response matching the shape of its scenarios' `expected`. Convention: /eval for a dedicated eval-mode handler that short-circuits side effects; agents that prefer to reuse /invoke may do so.

mode.description: deterministic — the endpoint promises reproducible outputs for the same input (short-circuited LLM / stubbed connectors); harness uses exact-match comparison. live — the endpoint uses real LLM / real connectors; harness uses fuzzy comparison (LLM-as-judge in future per ADR-044 §5a). deterministic is preferred for nightly runs — cheap, fast, honest.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-scenario timeout for the eval call.

scenarios.description: Agent-authored baseline scenarios. Each row is one test case: a question, a pre-resolved input payload, the expected response. The platform's install-time sync writes these into tenant_context_evaluation when the agent is installed on a tenant, scoped to the agent's package id. Tenants can add their own extra scenarios on top via the portal.

id.description: Stable identifier within the agent — survives version bumps so trend data stays attached to the same scenario.

cluster_tag.description: Scenario group tag — e.g. 'standard_refund', 'vip', 'adversarial'. Platform's health verdict groups by this to compute per-group pass rates.

question.description: Human-readable description of what this scenario tests. Shown in the portal's scenario list.

input.description: Pre-resolved input the harness POSTs to `endpoint` (deterministic mode); or payload for a real `/invoke` (live mode).

expected.description: Expected shape of the agent's response. deterministic mode: exact match on these keys. live mode: fuzzy / judge-model comparison.

config.description: JSON Schema for the agent's instance-level configuration. Portal renders a form from it when creating an instance.

network.description: Allowed egress hosts. Empty means kernel-network only.

callableAgents.description: Reverse-DNS ids of other agents this one may invoke.

errorCategory.description: The taxonomy the kernel classifies every failure into (ADR-011 §5). Manifest fields that reference categories must use these exact strings.
